mechanism_narrative: The sharp drop in TRANSIT, WORKPLACES, and RETAIL_REC together indicates voluntary avoidance of shared indoor activity; if that avoidance continues, retail-and-recreation mobility will keep falling over the next four weeks because people substitute away from discretionary outings.
failure_condition: If TRANSIT and WORKPLACES stabilize or rebound for two consecutive weeks but RETAIL_REC remains below its last-4-week mean by less than 5 points, this mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A new restriction or risk-response regime is implied when TRANSIT and WORKPLACES fall rapidly while RESIDENTIAL rises; under that threshold crossing, discretionary retail visits should drop further within one week and remain depressed for four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls below -25 points and WORKPLACES falls below -30 points
failure_condition: If TRANSIT is below -25 and WORKPLACES below -30 for at least one week but RETAIL_REC does not fall further in the following week, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: Weakening PARKS and GROCERY_PHARM mobility signals fewer out-of-home trips overall; because these errands precede discretionary shopping, the combined decline should pull RETAIL_REC down over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: If PARKS and GROCERY_PHARM both recover by at least 10 points from current levels yet RETAIL_REC does not improve over the next 14 days, the mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL rises while TRANSIT and WORKPLACES keep falling, households are staying home more and making fewer discretionary trips; that homebound substitution should keep RETAIL_REC below its recent average over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL rises above 12 points while TRANSIT remains below -20 points
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL stays above 12 while TRANSIT remains below -20 but RETAIL_REC rises above its last-4-week mean, this hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: A broad decline in PARKS alongside RETAIL_REC and TRANSIT is consistent with weather or calendar frictions reducing all nonessential trips; that shock should continue to suppress retail-and-recreation mobility over the next one to two weeks.
failure_condition: If PARKS rebounds strongly while RETAIL_REC remains flat or lower over the next week, the seasonal-friction explanation is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A threshold of unusually low TRANSIT combined with low WORKPLACES marks a commuting collapse that should mechanically reduce incidental retail stops with a lag; once both series cross that boundary, RETAIL_REC should fall further within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls below -30 points and WORKPLACES falls below -30 points
failure_condition: If both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES are below -30 for a week and RETAIL_REC does not decline over the next two weeks, the claim is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: The persistent rise in GROCERY_PHARM while RETAIL_REC falls suggests substitution toward essential errand-only travel; if this persists, discretionary retail mobility will remain weaker over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM recovers less than 5 points from baseline while RETAIL_REC rises above its prior 4-week mean, the substitution mechanism fails.

mechanism_narrative: If PARKS and GROCERY_PHARM both bottom out and begin recovering together, that signals broad mobility normalization that should spill over into retail visits within four weeks; the current collapse should therefore reverse only if both series turn up together.
candidate_trigger: PARKS and GROCERY_PHARM each rise by at least 8 points from their current week
failure_condition: If PARKS and GROCERY_PHARM both rise by at least 8 points but RETAIL_REC does not improve versus the last 28 days, the hypothesis is rejected.
